'''''Alcea rugosa''''', the '''Russian hollyhock''', is a species of flowering plant in the family [[Malvaceae]]. It is native to Ukraine, [[Crimea]], south European Russia, and the Caucasus, and has been introduced as a garden escapee into Wisconsin and Maryland in the United States.<ref name="558717-1" >{{cite web |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:558717-1 |title=''Alcea rugosa'' Alef. |author=<!--Not stated--> |website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=Board of Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date=21 August 2021 }}</ref> It is resistant to ''[[Puccinia malvacearum]]'' rust, and hardy to [[Hardiness zone|USDA zone 4]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=282569 |title=''Alcea rugosa'' |author=<!--Not stated--> |date= |website=Plant Finder |publisher=Missouri Botanical Garden |access-date=21 August 2021 }}</ref>
